agree.reason: The plain, respectful tone, the guaranteed pay and the offer to talk one on one give a wavering teller reasons to stay, but nothing speaks to tellers who don't want phone work, so a ten-year teller weighing severance may still leave.

honest.reason: Every number matches the brief, and the writer sensibly drops the unsupported claim that the change makes everyone's job better; 'hear this from me at the same time as everyone else' ignores two weeks of rumours, and 'not fair to colleagues' is a small addition the brief doesn't support.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are only restated; nothing is worked out, such as what severance means for a ten-year employee (20 weeks) or how the 8-to-8 rotation compares with a 40-hour week.

right_comparison.reason: It gives the trend (visits down 44%, contacts up 60%) and frames the choice for staff as the new role or severance, but never says what would happen to these branches if nothing changed.

qualification.reason: It names the uncertainty about rotating shifts and invites people to raise hours problems, but gives no decision deadline and doesn't say what happens if a scheduling need can't be met.

objections.reason: Longer hours and the loss of the branch and its members are taken on directly, but the main objection, 'I don't want to work on the phones,' gets only 'that's you,' and the rumours go unmentioned.

fit.reason: It is an email from the COO with clear sections at roughly 450 words, near the target; it deliberately softens the requested 'better for everyone' message, which costs a little on brief compliance.
